extracted.intended_audience: anthology editors; short-story authors; literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Selection and classification criteria used by an anthology editor (Edward J. O'Brien) to choose and rank the best American short stories published in magazines during a defined period (Jan–Oct 1918). Includes qualitative tests, grouping/marking system, and editorial rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The first test of a short story... is to report upon how vitally compelling the writer makes his selected facts or incidents. This test may be conveniently called the test of substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substance is something achieved by the artist in every act of creation rather than something already present; a fact or group of facts attains substantial embodiment only when the artist's power of compelling imaginative persuasion transforms them into a living truth. The editor used this as the first qualitative test when examining stories published in American periodicals during the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organic substance (must have 'pulse of life')
rubrics_metrics.description: No substance is of importance in fiction, unless it is organic substance, that is to say, substance in which the pulse of life is beating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inorganic fiction is identified as a curse; importance attaches only to 'organic' substance—material rendered imaginatively alive by the artist. Selection favors stories where life is palpably present in the material, not merely factual or mechanical incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of form
rubrics_metrics.description: The true artist will seek to shape this living substance into the most beautiful and satisfying form, by skilful selection and arrangement of his material, and by the most direct and appealing presentation of it in portrayal and characterization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form is the second necessary test for a story to take rank above others: how the writer arranges, selects, and presents material; effectiveness of portrayal and characterization; the aesthetic and satisfying organization of the story's material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological and imaginative reality / 'fresh living current'
rubrics_metrics.description: What has interested me... is the fresh living current which flows through the best of our work, and the psychological and imaginative reality which our writers have conferred upon it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for stories that convey believable psychology and vivid imaginative life; works that feel freshly alive rather than formulaic or merely topical. This quality is part of what the editor seeks when 'disengaging the essential human qualities' in fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of formulaic or dogmatic criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: I am not at all interested in formulae, and organized criticism at its best would be nothing more than dead criticism, as all dogmatic interpretation of life is always dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor avoids fixed formulas or rigid critical systems; values living, non-dogmatic judgment. This is guidance against applying mechanical checklists rather than qualitative, imaginative assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage selection: survive either or both tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories may survive either the test of substance or the test of form; some survive both tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that survive either test are worthy of distinction (see single asterisk); those that survive both rank higher (double asterisks). The editor explicitly recognizes that technique alone or persuasive sense of life alone can justify inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping and asterisk marking / Rolls of Honor
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are classified into four groups: (1) those that fail to survive either test (listed without comment); (2) those that survive either substance or form (indicated by a single asterisk); (3) those that survive both tests (indicated by two asterisks); (4) a small final group uniting genuine substance and artistic form in a closely woven pattern (indicated by three asterisks and listed in special 'Rolls of Honor').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-asterisk Roll of Honor forms the final source from which the stories reprinted in the volume were selected. The editor notes that some single asterisks in the Roll of Honor may also indicate a degree of personal preference (see next metric). The order of printed stories in the volume is alphabetical and not a ranking of comparative excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial rule: no republication of English stories or translations
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been a point of honor with me not to republish an English story, nor a translation from a foreign author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection limited to American original stories (published in American periodicals) — the editor excludes reprinting English or translated foreign works in this anthology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial rule: one story per author in the volume
rubrics_metrics.description: I have also made it a rule not to include more than one story by an individual author in the volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures breadth of authors represented; influences selection when multiple strong stories by one author exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal and source scope of selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The present record covers the period from January to October inclusive, 1918. During the past ten months I have sought to select from the stories published in American magazines those which have rendered life imaginatively in organic substance and artistic form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is limited to stories published in American periodicals within a defined calendar window; the Yearbook also compiles indices (magazine addresses, biographical rolls, best books, critical summaries) to document coverage and make the selection transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection objective: 'disengaging the essential human qualities' — a 'criticism of life'
rubrics_metrics.description: I have set myself the task of disengaging the essential human qualities in our contemporary fiction which, when chronicled conscientiously by our literary artists, may fairly be called a criticism of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary evaluative aim is to identify fiction that offers honest, human insight; the anthology prefers works that function as a 'criticism of life' rather than merely entertainment or skilled craft detached from human significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality with acknowledgement of personal preference
rubrics_metrics.description: In compiling these lists, I have permitted no personal preference or prejudice to influence my judgment consciously for or against a story. To the titles of certain stories, however, in the 'Rolls of Honor,' an asterisk is prefixed, and this asterisk, I must confess, reveals in some measure a personal preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor aims at objectivity but transparently admits that some selections reflect personal taste; marks indicating such preferences are documented in the indices.
